task: explain why eight gate tests passed alone and failed in the full suite

inputs.symptom: test_wiring_cycle 8 failed in-suite, 19 passed alone; the gate reported 'no candidate beat the incumbent' for a candidate forced to win by 0.5
inputs.probe: a temporary test loaded immediately before the file printed wc_wg_is_test_wg=false and wg_is_sysmod=false

label.root_cause: worm_registry._purge_worm_modules() deletes EVERY CORE.WORMS.* entry from sys.modules so the @register_worm decorators re-fire; helper modules (wiring_genome) therefore come back as DIFFERENT module objects. A test that patches its own module-level import patches an object the cycle never calls. The purge's docstring warns only about worm CLASS identity
label.fix: tests patch the module the cycle actually calls (_cycle_wg(mod)) plus a regression test that loads the cycle AFTER a reset and asserts the gate still gates

task: explain 69 collection errors in the full suite

inputs.guard: CORE/sentinel_enforcer.py installs a process-global sys.addaudithook at import that raises PermissionError on open(...w/a/+/x) without a thread-local token
inputs.mitigation: tests/conftest.py held the token per test with a FUNCTION-scoped autouse fixture
inputs.failures: 207 PermissionErrors; 69 collection errors in test_evolution_gates (61) and test_import_map (8); both files pass alone

label.root_cause: pytest sets up module/class-scoped fixtures BEFORE function-scoped ones, so a module-scoped fixture importing scripts/evolution_cycle.py (which opens its log file at line 48) was blocked before the permit ran
label.fix: a pytest_runtest_setup hook latches the token open (earliest hook a conftest gets, before fixture setup of any scope) and is left on for the session

evidence.detected_by: reproduced with pytest tests/test_compliance_step45_init.py tests/test_evolution_gates.py -> 25 passed, 61 errors
evidence.verified: same prefix plus test_import_map.py -> 105 passed, 0 errors
